hooks.command:
jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.filePath' | { read -r f; case "$f" in *.hs|*/docs/*.md) echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","additionalContext":"STOP. MANDATORY CHECKLIST — answer each before proceeding:
1. OLD CODE: Check old sasha code for the pattern FIRST, but DO NOT blindly copy — old code has broken parts. Show the user the pattern you found and ASK before applying it.
2. SCOPE: Did the user ask for this specific change? If not, STOP. Do not show initiative, do not make extra changes.
3. NoImplicitPrelude: ON in ALL packages. Do not use Prelude names without explicit imports.
4. IMPORTS: Explicit imports ONLY — list every name, no wildcards (..).
5. QUALIFIED: No qualified imports unless name collision — then qualifier is the module name, no aliases.
6. LENSES: Use view/set/over from Lens.Micro.Platform — NEVER direct record field access.
7. TOTALITY: No partial patterns — no head, no [x] = expr, handle all branches.
8. NEWTYPES: No naked types — use newtypes for domain values, never raw Text/Int/String.
9. NO STUBS: No placeholders, no TODOs, no fake implementations. If you cannot write real code, STOP and say so.
10. NO DEBATE: Do not second-guess the user. Apply the instruction. If it fails, come back with the compiler error.
11. HLINT: Do not debate hlint suggestions — apply them.
12. HACKAGE FIRST: Check Hackage BEFORE inventing any type — Data.Time for dates, Warp for Port, etc.
13. LIBRARIES: Must match reference codebases (sasha, quux/server, ix).
14. MINIMAL: No redundant abstractions. No reinvented types. No extra changes beyond what was asked.
15. FORMATTING: Do NOT reformat surrounding content. Minimal targeted edits only.
16. INSTANCE IMPORTS: If you change an import to (), justify why — name the specific instance it provides. If you cannot, delete the import entirely."}}'; ;; *) echo '{}'; ;; esac; }
